title: CLI Help, File Loading & Argument Parsing Epic
description:
Full CLI argument parsing overhaul for the Lisp VM.

The current CLI has no argument parsing — it always enters REPL mode regardless of input flags. This epic covers:
- `--help` / `-h` flag with formatted usage output
- `--version` / `-v` flag with version display
- `-f` / `--file` flag for loading and executing Lisp source files (repeatable)
- Positional file argument as alternative to `-f`
- Proper error handling for unknown flags, missing arguments, and invalid inputs

All changes are documented in the openspec change: openspec/changes/cli-help.md
design:
See openspec/changes/cli-help.md for full design document.

Key design decisions:
- Use std.process.args for simple argument parsing (no external library)
- PrintHelp helper function with formatted multiline string
- File execution order: -f flags in order, then positional file, then REPL
- Exit codes: 0 for success, 1 for errors
- --help and --version short-circuit all other processing
close_reason: All tasks completed

title: Implement --help / -h flag with formatted output
description:
Add --help and -h flag support to the CLI. When triggered, prints a formatted usage message and exits cleanly with code 0.

The help message includes:
- Usage line: `Usage: lisp-vm [OPTIONS] [FILE]`
- One-line description
- Available options table
- Examples section

--help should be processable even after other flags (e.g., `--help -f file.lisp` still shows help).
design:
```zig
fn printHelp(program: []const u8) void {
    const help = \Usage: {s} [OPTIONS] [FILE]


        \A minimal Lisp bytecode VM.


        \Options:

        \  -h, --help       Show this help message

        \  -v, --version    Show version

        \  -f, --file FILE  Load and execute a Lisp source file


        \Examples:

        \  {s}                  Start interactive REPL

        \  {s} --help           Show help

        \  {s} -f program.lisp  Run a Lisp file
;
    ;
    debugPrint(help, .{ program, program, program, program });
}
```

In main(), parse args and check for -h/--help before any other processing.
Call printHelp(progName) and return.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `./zig-out/bin/lisp-vm --help` prints formatted help and exits with code 0
- [ ] `./zig-out/bin/lisp-vm -h` produces the same output
- [ ] Help message includes Usage line, Options section, Examples section
- [ ] `--help` works even when other flags follow (e.g., `--help -f foo`)
- [ ] Exit code is 0
close_reason: Implemented in commit 47a3645

title: Fix quote evaluation: produces dotted pairs instead of proper lists
description:
## Problem

(quote (1 2 3)) produces (1 . (2 . 3)) instead of a proper list (1 . (2 . (3 . nil))). Same bug affects all quoted lists.

## Root Cause

In _buildConsList (line ~2163 in src/root.zig), the last AST element is incorrectly used as the final cdr instead of nil.

src/root.zig - _buildConsList function (line ~2163)

title: Create a Standard Library for the Lisp VM
description:
## Goal

Build a standard library of common Lisp functions that are missing from the core VM. These will be provided as Lisp code files (not built-in Zig primitives) that can be loaded with the  builtin.

## Scope

The standard library should provide common higher-level Lisp functions as user-space definitions that rely on the core primitives (defn, def, if, let, cons, car, cdr, null?, length, append, map, filter, etc.).

## Initial Functionality

Priority P0 (essential):
- list — create a list from arguments
- first/second/third — access by index  
- last — get the last element of a list
- butlast — all but the last element
- reverse — reverse a list
- member? — check if element is in a list
- assoc — association lookup in an alist
- flatten — flatten nested lists

Priority P1 (useful):
- sort — general-purpose sorting
- mapcar — map over list
- reduce/reduce-right — fold operations
- apply — apply function to argument list
- eval — evaluate an expression
- eq — structural equality
- evenp/oddp — predicate helpers
- abs — absolute value
- max/min — max/min of numbers

## How to Use

1. Create an epic with this description
2. Use 📋 Ready work (1 issue with no blockers):

1. [● P1] [bug] sqhn-y6o: Fix quote evaluation: produces dotted pairs instead of proper lists to discover tasks under this epic
3. Each task should implement one or more functions
4. Implementations go in a .lisp file (e.g., examples/stdlib.lisp or stdlib/stdlib.lisp)
5. Tests should verify each function works correctly

## Files to Create

- stdlib/stdlib.lisp — the standard library implementation
- src/root.zig — add tests for new functions
- examples/ — example programs using the library

## Acceptance Criteria

- All initial P0 functions implemented and tested
- All functions work correctly with edge cases (empty lists, nil, nested structures)
- No memory leaks (GC handles everything properly)
- 100% test coverage for stdlib functions
- Functions follow consistent naming conventions (Lisp style with ? suffix for predicates)

title: Document Zig bytecode arena reuse anti-pattern and clear() fix
description:
When writing bytecode tests, NEVER reuse a Bytecode instance via deinit() → reinit() — the 'defer bc.deinit()' at function scope captures the variable by value and double-frees on the second deinit, causing signal ABRT.

The fix: Bytecode.clear() zeroes all arrays (ops, constants, closure_bodies) without freeing, retaining allocator capacity for reuse within the same arena. Use bc.clear() between test cases.

Example of wrong pattern:
  bc.deinit();
  bc = Bytecode.init(alloc);
  defer bc.deinit();  // double-free crash!

Correct pattern:
  bc.clear();  // safe, retains capacity

See commit be3d5e1.
